content.thinking:
I’ve just finished laying down the core engine pieces that the game will need: the type effectiveness chart, the input handling, audio synthesis, and the graphics generation utilities. Those files are all in place under the `js` folder, and the HTML scaffold is already serving the canvas. The asset fetcher has also populated the sprites and data files, so the static resources are ready.

The next logical chunk of the Pokémon system is the mechanics that drive the battle and overworld behavior. After type chart, the engine still needs to know how a Pokémon’s stats are derived from its base stats, IVs, EVs, level, and nature. It also needs the experience curve formulas to determine level‑up timing, the move‑learning tables for each species, the evolution conditions, and finally the item catalog that will be used for healing, evolution stones, held items, etc.

All of these pieces are closely related: stat calculation depends on the base stats that are stored in the pokédex data, experience curves are defined per growth rate (also in the pokédex), move learning ties into the moves data, and evolution references both moves and items. By announcing that I’m moving on to “Pokémon logic — stat calculation, exp curves, move learning, evolution, plus the item catalog,” I’m signaling the next development phase clearly to the user and setting up the expectation for the subsequent files I’ll create. This is the natural next step before diving into the actual implementation code for these systems.
